seesaw.notes: The a and b jacks and the two outputs carry whatever is patched in, so they are given no family. The steps CV inputs take the floor of the voltage, so 2.9V is two steps. The button and the jack for clock are added together before one Schmitt trigger, and the same for reset (src/seesaw.cpp:71-72), so a press while the jack already reads above 1V does nothing. The maker's tooltips on the step CV inputs already say 0-10V, 1V/step, and the code agrees.

notepad.notes: The panel abbreviates the intervals (m2, M2, tri, oct, 2tri, 2oct and so on) while the maker's tooltips spell them out; the lines use the spelled-out names. The loop runs over every output index, so the semitone offset is exactly the output's index and the jack the maker calls octave tritone is eighteen semitones, an augmented eleventh. Only channel 1 of a poly cable is read.

prismo.notes: The step jacks and the row outputs carry whatever is patched in, so they are given no family. The steps CV takes the floor of the voltage and is clamped up to 1, so anything below 1V gives a single step. The step lamps are lights rather than params and cannot be clicked. The maker's step jack tooltips read a one, a two and so on; the panel prints the row letter in brackets down the left and the step names across the top.
